images.title: Many names for one half
images.purpose: Show that when each half of a watermelon is cut into equal slices, the slices in one half give a fraction equal to 1/2, with the bottom number twice the top.
images.composition: Three round watermelon slices of the same size in a row with wide gaps, each with its fraction under it, and one pattern line centred below.
images.exact_structure: Three flat round watermelon slices seen from above, all exactly the same size, plain rind outline. Circle 1: cut into 8 equal wedges, the left 4 wedges filled teal #0072B2. Circle 2: cut into 10 equal wedges, the left 5 wedges filled teal. Circle 3: cut into 12 equal wedges, the left 6 wedges filled teal. In every circle the shaded wedges make exactly the left half, split by a vertical reddish purple #CC79A7 line. No seeds drawn. Exactly 3 circles, 8, 10 and 12 wedges.
labels: bottom number is twice the top

images.takeaway: 4/8, 5/10 and 6/12 all equal 1/2: the bottom number is twice the top.
images.description: Three same-size watermelon slices cut into 8, 10 and 12 equal wedges; the left half of each is teal, labelled 4/8, 5/10 and 6/12, each equal to 1/2.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to count the teal wedges and all the wedges in each slice, and say the bottom number is twice the top.

image_decisions.why: Cutting each half into more slices is a picture idea; one image of three cut circles carries it.
